title: Root-cause fix: git_reachable() tested object existence, not ancestry (found during TC-27b)
evidence_refs: Found live during the font/python canary (TC-27b): direct check_freshness("font","python") returned CURRENT (silently) instead of the mandatory-acceptance-criterion-#3 HISTORY_REWRITTEN_CONTENT_IDENTICAL, despite TC-11 claiming this exact scenario was fixed and tested

Root cause: baseline_resolver.git_reachable() used git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit} (tests OBJECT EXISTENCE) instead of git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> HEAD (tests ANCESTRY/reachability) -- a history-rewritten orphan commit stays a dangling-but-present loose object until garbage-collected, so cat-file -e wrongly reported it reachable. Confirmed live against font/pythons real clone: cat-file -e exit 0, merge-base --is-ancestor exit 1, same sha same repo.

Why TC-11s own test suite missed this: its _rewrite_history_with_fresh_root_commit helper deliberately does a FULL git re-init (docstring explicitly says why: to avoid leaving the old object cat-file-visible) -- so its reproduction never actually exercised the real dangling-object condition, only a case where the object is genuinely gone

Fix: git_reachable() now uses merge-base --is-ancestor. Added a live-git fallback (_orphaned_commit_tree_sha) in freshness_guard._check_baseline_reachability for pre-TC-10 ledger entries with no recorded repo_tree_sha (fonts real case) -- the dangling orphan objects tree is still directly rev-parse-able

2 new regression tests added (test_baseline_resolver.py, test_freshness_guard.py) using git commit --amend to reproduce the real dangling-but-present shape; both fail against the pre-fix code, pass against the fix
